description: Agent Aviation Records: submit aircraft maintenance records with the mechanic, fleet and part records they answer to: each aircraft the fleet record lists with its id, tail number and type; each mechanic and certificate record with its id, reference, name, certificate number and the moment the certificate expires; each part record with its id, reference, part number and the source record the part came with; each maintenance log entry with its id, reference, tail number, the work performed, the mechanic, the certificate it cites, the moment signed off, the airframe total hours at sign-off, the parts installed and the interval in hours or days it states until the task is next due. The signed report gives the entries and the records behind them, each entry against a mechanic record holding a certificate in force on the day signed off, each entry’s aircraft against the fleet record, each part installed against a part record naming its source, and each repeat of a task against the interval the earlier entry states, and counts them, and names divergent maintenance records: a maintenance entry with no mechanic or certificate record behind it, work recorded on an aircraft the fleet record does not list, a part recorded as installed with no part or source record behind it, and maintenance recorded past the interval the record itself states; then a task done again after an entry stating no interval and an entry recording no work, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No entries, no mechanic records beside entries, no fleet record beside entries that name an aircraft, or no part records beside parts installed leaves those points unverified. Tail numbers, certificates and parts match by letters and digits, a part matches by its record reference or part number, mechanics match by record reference or name, a certificate expires after the day it states, tasks match by their words on one aircraft, and a repeat runs past its interval when more hours or days than the earlier entry states have passed. This reads whether every maintenance entry was signed off by a certificated mechanic, on a listed aircraft, with sourced parts and inside its interval. Verdict aviation_maintenance_log_divergent, aviation_maintenance_log_partial, aviation_maintenance_log_unverified or aviation_maintenance_log_consistent. POST /api/aviation-maintenance-log-check. Reads the aviation records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it flies no aircraft, inspects no aircraft in person, contacts no regulator, examiner or maintenance provider and issues no certification, which stay with the operator, its pilots, its mechanics and its regulators, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Aviation Records reads an air operator’s own records: flight log records, aircraft maintenance records, airworthiness and directive records, inspection records, pilot certificate records, training and currency records, flight duty and rest records and incident report records, each against the fleet, maintenance, pilot and duty records, the mechanic, certificate and part records, the flight log and the maintenance record, the aircraft, operations and dates flown, the schedule and the corrective entries, the required events and the currency records, the operator’s own limits, or the follow-up entries on record. The family’s ground is the paper trail behind the aircraft and the crew: what the flight log shows, what the maintenance record supports, what the certificates cover, and whether the duty and incident records hold up; it reads records about aircraft and crews, not live flight tracking and not travel booking: the Agent Travel family reads the bookings behind a trip, the Agent Agriculture Records family reads a farm’s production records and the Agent Food Safety Records family reads a food business’s safety file, while this family reads an air operator’s own records and reads none of those. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-aviation-records-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-aviation-records/.

at.description: When signed off, such as 2026-03-02 or 2026-03-02T14:30Z.

certificate.description: The certificate number the entry cites.

interval_days.description: Days the entry states until the task is next due.

interval_hours.description: Hours the entry states until the task is next due.

mechanic.description: The mechanic, by reference or name.

parts.description: Part numbers or part records installed.

fleet.description: Each aircraft the fleet record lists.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

expires_at.description: When the certificate expires, such as 2026-03-02 or 2026-03-02T14:30Z.

source.description: The source record the part came with.
